title: Trail mix with nuts and fruit

content.title: About
content.content: Trail mix with nuts and fruit is a combination of various nuts (almonds, cashews, walnuts, etc.) and dried fruits (raisins, cranberries, apricots, etc.). This snack is popular among hikers and athletes because of its high energy density, portability, and diverse flavors.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The term “trail mix” originated in the United States in the early 20th century to describe a snack taken on hikes.
The blend of nuts and dried fruit provides a quick glucose boost from the fruit and a sustained release of energy from the nuts’ fats.
In some countries chocolate chips or yogurt coating are added for extra taste.
Nuts in the mix are often lightly roasted with a pinch of salt or spices to enhance aroma.
Dried fruits can be dehydrated without added sugar, preserving their natural sweetness.

items.title: Energy support
items.content: The mix delivers both rapid and prolonged energy, useful during long physical activities.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Nuts contain monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Both nuts and dried fruits provide vitamin E, magnesium, potassium, iron, and dietary fiber.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Fiber from the fruits and nuts promotes regular bowel function.

items.title: Antioxidant effect
items.content: Phytonutrients in nuts and berries (e.g., cranberries) help combat free radicals.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: The mix contains multiple nuts that can trigger severe allergic reactions.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because of its fat content, the mix is calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Dried fruits are naturally sweet, raising the overall sugar level; people with diabetes should choose unsweetened versions.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Small nuts and dried fruit pieces can pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Trail mix is convenient to carry on hikes, workouts, or to the office as a quick snack. It can be added to yogurt, oatmeal, salads, or eaten straight from the bag. For extra flavor, lightly toast the nuts with sea salt or spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the mix in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator to prevent the nuts from going rancid.
